brief.subject: FTC strikes back at imposters; health plan pitches under fire
brief.headline: FTC Removes 19 Fake FTC Websites as Imposter Scams Stay on Top
brief.dek: The FTC reports progress against impersonators, warns health plan marketers during open enrollment, and sues Dollar General over register prices.
brief.lede: The FTC says it has taken down 19 websites pretending to be the agency. Its enforcement has returned more than $80 million to consumers since its Impersonation Rule took effect in 2024.

sections.heading: Fake FTC Sites Taken Down
bullets: 19 websites posing as the FTC have been removed, so scammers keep borrowing the agency's name to look official.
More than $80 million in consumer refunds came from FTC impersonation cases since the 2024 rule took effect.
The FTC calls imposter scams the top reported fraud category, so treat surprise calls from 'officials' with suspicion.
Hang up and contact the agency yourself using a number you look up independently, never one the caller provides.

sections.heading: Health Plan Pitches Get Warnings
bullets: 25 companies selling or generating leads for health plans received FTC warning letters during open enrollment.
The letters flag claims about plan terms that may be deceptive, so double-check coverage details before signing up.
More letters will follow on a rolling basis, signaling the FTC is still watching this busy sales season.

sections.heading: Dollar General Sued Over Prices
bullets: The FTC and 20 states allege Dollar General charged more at checkout than shelf tags and ads showed.
Regulators say the overcharges cost shoppers millions of dollars, so comparing your receipt to posted prices is worth the effort.

sections.heading: Your Data May Set Your Price
bullets: Nine airlines, ride-share and food-delivery firms were ordered to explain how personal data shapes what customers pay.
The FTC inquiry could reveal whether two shoppers see different prices for the same service.

brief.seo_description: FTC removes 19 fake FTC websites, warns 25 health plan marketers during open enrollment, and sues Dollar General with 20 states over pricing.
